sources.title: Hans-Jürgen Schneider, Lectures on Hopf algebras, notes by Sonia Natale
sources.locator: Complete 56-page lecture-note PDF. Focused §1 printed pp. 2–8 for definitions, tensor product structures, and examples; Proposition 1.4 printed p. 14; Theorem 1.5(a)–(c) printed pp. 15–16.

contents.name: Tensor-product coalgebra maps
contents.reason: The local lemma defines the middle-factor flip and proves coassociativity and both counit equations on finite tensor sums.

contents.name: Bialgebra structure and map compatibility
contents.reason: The definition states all algebra, coalgebra and structure-map data locally.

contents.name: Algebra-map versus coalgebra-map compatibility
contents.reason: The local proof expands all four structure equations and proves both implications.

contents.name: Associativity and unit of convolution
contents.reason: The local proof supplies the threefold-coalgebra calculation and both unit contractions without a dimension assumption.

contents.name: Hopf algebra and antipode definition
contents.reason: The definition identifies the antipode as the two-sided convolution inverse and states no composition-inverse requirement.

contents.name: Antipode uniqueness and anti-map identities
contents.reason: The local proof gives both convolution-inverse calculations for multiplication and comultiplication and proves the unit and counit identities.

contents.name: Group, finite-function, and polynomial Hopf structures
contents.reason: The local proof checks the maps on group bases, polynomial generators/monomials, and finite function evaluations.

contents.name: Commutative and cocommutative involutivity branches
contents.reason: The two hypotheses are handled separately by explicit convolution calculations using anti-multiplicativity.

sources.title: Pavel Etingof and Mykola Semenyakin, A brief introduction to quantum groups
sources.locator: Complete 43-page lecture-note PDF. Focused §§2.1.2–2.2.2, PDF pp. 2–5: finite-group functions, Hopf axioms, antipode properties and group/primitive examples.

contents.name: Finite-group function algebra formulas
contents.reason: The item verifies the finite-set tensor identification and all Hopf equations locally.

contents.name: Group algebra structure and cocommutativity
contents.reason: The item proves the construction for arbitrary groups by linear extension from the group basis.

contents.name: Primitive generators and characteristic-dependent polynomial behavior
contents.reason: The example proves the characteristic-zero and positive-characteristic calculations explicitly.

contents.name: Antipode anti-homomorphism and uniqueness statements
contents.reason: The theorem supplies local inverse calculations rather than relying on the source's assertion.

contents.name: Commutative/cocommutative involutivity and its limits
contents.reason: The item proves the two sufficient branches and does not promote involutivity to the general definition.

sources.title: Thomas Rüd, Hopf Algebras and rooted trees, Practical work in mathematics
sources.locator: Complete 32-page PDF. Focused §2.3.1–2.4, PDF pp. 9–12: convolution, bialgebra equivalence, Hopf definition and uniqueness.

contents.name: Bialgebra compatibility equivalence
contents.reason: The local proof states the four equations and checks the multiplication and unit coalgebra-map conditions directly.

contents.name: Convolution algebra
contents.reason: The local proof supplies the associativity and unit computations in full.

contents.name: Hopf definition and antipode uniqueness
contents.reason: The definition specifies convolution as the relevant inverse operation; the example demonstrates the distinction from composition.

contents.name: Group-algebra Hopf example
contents.reason: The local proof verifies every group-algebra structure map and antipode equation.

companions.reason: The three companion calculations are proved locally from the A-page Hopf structures and finite algebraic computations; the A-page sources provide context, not substitute proofs.
